        APPLICATION OF OKLAHOMA GAS AND ELECTRIC COMPANY
      FOR AUTHORITY TO ISSUE SHORT-TERM DEBT SECURITIES UNDER
               SECTION 204 OF THE FEDERAL POWER ACT

           Oklahoma Gas and Electric Company, an Oklahoma corporation (herein called

the “Company”) and a public utility as defined in Section 201 of the Federal Power Act, 1

hereby submits this application (“Application”) to the Federal Energy Regulatory

Commission (“FERC”), pursuant to Section 204 of the Federal Power Act 2 and Part 34 of

the FERC’s regulations, 3 for the issuance of an order no later than December 1, 2026

authorizing the Company to issue from time to time during the period ending December

31, 2028, short-term debt securities with a final maturity date no later than December 31,

2029, and in amounts so that the aggregate principal amount outstanding at any one time

shall not exceed $1,500,000,000.

      I.       Contents of Application

           In support of its Application and in accordance with the provisions of Part 34 of

the FERC’s regulations, the Company states as follows:

(a)        The official name of the applicant and address of its principal business office:

                     Oklahoma Gas and Electric Company
                     321 North Harvey
                     Oklahoma City, Oklahoma 73101-0321

 (b)     The State in which the utility is incorporated, the date of incorporation and each
        State in which it operates:

        The Company was incorporated under the laws of the Territory of Oklahoma on

February 27, 1902, and has been duly qualified as a foreign corporation in Arkansas. The

Company operates in the States of Oklahoma and Arkansas.

(c)     The name, address and telephone number of a person within the utility authorized
        to receive notices and communications with respect to the Application:

                                          Jason D. Bailey

(d)     The date by which Commission action is requested:

        The Company requests that Commission action be taken with respect to this

Application by December 1, 2026.

(e)     A full description of the securities proposed to be issued including:

        (1)      Type and nature of securities.

        Within the limits set forth in this Application, the Company proposes and seeks

authority to issue promissory notes and other evidences of indebtedness, including

guarantees (the “Short-term Debt”). All Short-term Debt would mature in one year or

less from its date of issuance, 4 and the Short-term Debt would be expected to include, but

not be limited to, promissory notes issued to commercial banks and institutional

investors, intercompany loans from affiliates, promissory notes issued and sold to




4
         The issuance and placement of Short-term Debt as described in this Application are not subject to
competitive bidding and negotiated placement requirements of Section 34.2(a) of FERC’s regulations
because the Short-term Debt matures within one year or less of issuance and thus is exempt from those
requirements pursuant to Section 34.2(b)(3) of FERC’s regulations.


                                                    2
 commercial paper dealers, commercial paper issued and sold directly to persons

(including trust departments of commercial banks) who customarily purchase commercial

paper for their own accounts, drafts and other evidences of indebtedness issued and sold

to banks and other institutional investors, which, in the case of banks, may be accepted

and resold as bankers’ acceptances and guarantees of any of the foregoing.

        (2)     Amount of securities (par or stated value and number of units).

        The Company seeks authority to issue from time to time through December 31,

2028, and to have outstanding at any one time up to $1.5 billion of Short-term Debt. All

the Short-term Debt would mature in one year or less from its date of issuance and,

accordingly, would mature on or before December 31, 2029.

        (3)     Interest or dividend rate, if any.

        The interest rate applicable to the Short-term Debt would be no greater than the

highest of: (i) the prime rate announced by Wells Fargo National Association, the

administrative agent under the Company’s credit facility, plus a credit spread of up to 200

basis points; (ii) the federal funds effective rate at the time of issuance, plus a credit

spread of up to 200 basis points; or (iii) the six month term Secured Overnight Financing

Rate as published by CME Group Benchmark Administration Limited plus a credit

spread of up to 200 basis points. The interest rate for the Short-term Debt issued as

commercial paper will be based on the market interest rate as of the date of issuance of

commercial paper of comparable quality and comparable maturity sold to domestic

commercial paper dealers and shall not exceed the maximum interest rate described

above. The Pro Forma Interest and Interest Coverage calculations in the attached

Exhibits C, D, and E apply the maximum interest rate for multi-day borrowing using the

methodology described above, to a hypothetical borrowing of the full amount of the


                                               3
 requested authorization. The combined interest coverage calculation provided in Exhibit

E to this application assumes the prime rate plus a margin of 200 basis points.

       (4)     Dates of issuance and maturity:

       The Short-term Debt will be issued from time to time through December 31,

2028. All the Short-term Debt would mature in one year or less from its date of issuance

and, accordingly, would mature on or before December 31, 2029.

       (5)     Institutional rating of securities- or if the securities are not rated, an
               explanation as to why they are not rated, and if the securities will be rated
               an estimate of the rating.

       The Company’s short-term issuer ratings are A2, P2, and F2 by Standard and

Poor’s, Moody’s, and Fitch, respectively.

       (6)     Any stock exchange on which the securities will be listed.

       The Short-term Debt will not be listed on any stock exchange.

(f)    The purpose for which the securities for which application is made are to be
       issued:

               (1)     If the purpose of such issuance is the construction, completion,
                       extension, or improvement of facilities, describe in reasonable
                       detail the construction program for which the funds were or are to
                       be used.

               (2)     If the purpose for such issuance is for the refunding of obligations,
                       describe in detail the obligations to be refunded, including the
                       character, principal amounts, applicable discount or premium,
                       dates of issuance and maturity, and all other material facts
                       concerning such obligations.

               (3)     If the purpose for such issuance is for other than construction or
                       refunding, explain such other purpose(s) in detail.

       The principal purposes for which the Company will issue and sell Short-term

Debt are: (1) to carry accounts receivable; (2) to provide for periodic large cash needs,

such as tax, dividend and interest payments; (3) to purchase and carry fuel inventories;




                                             4
 (4) to supply temporary funds for unexpected cash requirements; (5) to provide

temporary financing of current transactions; (6) to provide interim financing for the

construction of additions to the Company’s generation, transmission and distribution

facilities; (7) to provide temporary financing of possible acquisitions of additions and

extensions to the Company’s plant and service territory; (8) to provide interim financing

for the purchase of other assets or the purchase or redemption of the Company’s

securities; (9) to provide temporary financing for economic development projects in the

Company’s service territory; (10) to provide cash on a temporary basis to existing and

future affiliates of the Company for working capital purposes; and (11) to renew or

refund other Short-term Debt that was issued for one of the foregoing reasons.

       Although eleven principal purposes have been listed for the issuance and sale of

Short-term Debt, a key purpose is to provide interim financing in connection with the

Company’s construction and capacity acquisition program. The Company’s total capital

expenditures for 2027 and 2028 are estimated to be $3.055 billion. The amounts of such

expenditures, including allowance for funds used during construction for each of such

years, are estimated as follows:

                                                            2027                        2028
    Transmission                          $                    310            $            305
    Oklahoma distribution                 $                    705            $            725
    Arkansas distribution                 $                     25            $             25
    Generation reliability                $                    160            $            165
    Generation capacity projects          $                    190            $            165
    Technology, fleet & facilities        $                    135            $            145

       Total                              $                  1,525            $          1,530




                                              5
         The Company’s construction and capital expenditure plans are revised from time

to time to reflect changes in customer demand, business and economic conditions,

regulations and laws, the cost and availability of capital and other factors.

        Another key purpose for the issuance and sale of Short-term Debt is the possible

redemption of outstanding long-term debt, which is callable. In each instance, the

Company would expect to refinance on a permanent basis the debt to be redeemed

through the issuance of a new series of long-term debt with a lower effective interest cost

to the Company. However, to reduce its overall cost of capital, the Company may

redeem an outstanding series of long-term debt and finance such redemption temporarily

through the use of Short-term Debt pending the issuance of a new series of long-term

debt. The Company has not determined the outstanding long-term debt it will seek to

redeem, as this decision will depend on financial market conditions and, in particular,

interest rates.

        Although the Company does not presently expect to have all the $1.5 billion of

Short-term Debt outstanding at any one time through the end of 2028, the Company

believes that it must have the flexibility and the authority to have up to $1.5 billion of

Short-term Debt outstanding during that period. The Company’s estimates of

construction and capital expenditures and internally generated funds are based on certain

key assumptions that could change significantly over the next several years.

Furthermore, there can be no assurance that the Company’s receipt of revenues from its

operations will coincide simultaneously with its need to pay expenditures or its desire to

redeem outstanding long-term debt. Therefore, it is necessary that the Company have

maximum flexibility to finance its activities on an interim basis pending receipt of cash




                                              6
 from its operations and to respond to changing conditions that may affect its ability to

fund its future construction and other capital needs. Uncertainties that may substantially

affect the degree to which construction and other requirements can be met by funds

provided by operations include such items as the impact of inflation on operating

expenses and construction costs, the level of kilowatt-hour sales, the demand from other

utilities for interchange power, new environmental legislation and regulations, and the

actions of the various regulatory commissions that set the Company’s electric rates.

       In addition to the sale of long-term debt described above to refinance outstanding

long-term debt, financing of its operations also requires the Company from time to time

to engage in sales of other permanent securities, including debt, preferred stock and

common stock. Such sales of permanent securities are normally scheduled when it is

anticipated that accumulated short term borrowings are large enough to justify permanent

financing. The permanent financing of short-term borrowings, on occasion, may be

delayed for varying periods of time because of unfavorable market conditions for long-

term financing. Accordingly, the Company also must be able to continue to finance its

operations on an interim basis under such circumstances until market conditions warrant

the issuance of permanent securities.

       The sale by the Company of permanent securities requires certain regulatory

approvals. The Company’s sale of common stock, of debt with a maturity of more than

one year and of preferred stock must be authorized by the Oklahoma Corporation

Commission (“OCC”) and, in certain instances, the Arkansas Public Service Commission

(“APSC”).




                                             7
 (g)     A statement as to whether or not any application with respect to the transaction or
        any part thereof is required to be filed with any State regulatory body:

        No Federal or State regulatory body, other than the FERC, has jurisdiction over

the issuance of the Short-term Debt referred to in this Application.

(h)     A detailed statement of the facts relied upon by the applicant to show the
        issuance: (1) is for some lawful object, within the corporate purposes of the
        applicant and compatible with the public interest, is necessary or appropriate for
        or consistent with the proper performances by the applicant of service as a public
        utility and will not impair its ability to perform that service; and (2) is reasonably
        necessary or appropriate for such purposes:

        As described above, proceeds from the issuance of the Short-term Debt are

expected to be used for the purposes identified in item (f) above, including to provide

interim financing of the Company’s construction and capital expenditure program. This

construction and capital expenditure program is essential to enable the Company to meet

its public utility responsibilities and to serve the increasing reliability and capacity

requirements of its customers. The use of Short-term Debt maturing in one year or less

from the date of issuance will provide the Company with a vital interim financing

medium. When used in conjunction with long-term financing, it will provide additional

sources of credit and will significantly increase the Company’s flexibility in meeting its

financing requirements under the money market conditions now prevailing. In addition,

the laws of Oklahoma under which the Company is organized, and the Restated

Certificate of Incorporation of the Company permit the Company to issue its securities

for proper corporate purposes, including the purposes set forth in item (f) above. The

Company represents, therefore, that the issuance of the Short-term Debt:

                        (i)     is for a lawful object within its corporate purposes and
                                compatible with the public interest, is necessary or
                                appropriate for or consistent with the proper performance
                                by the Company of service as a public utility and will not
                                impair the Company’s ability to perform that service; and


                                               8
                          (ii)     is reasonably necessary or appropriate for such purposes.

        The Company also agrees that any Short-term Debt issued pursuant to the

authorization requested in this Application will be subject to the four restrictions on such

securities specified in the Commission’s Westar order. 5

(i)     A detailed statement of bond indenture(s) or other limitations on interest and
        dividend coverage, and the effects of such limitations on the issuance of
        additional debt or equity securities:

        The Company currently has no preferred stock outstanding. The Company’s

Restated Certificate of Incorporation contains provisions governing the issuance of

preferred stock. These provisions in substance provide that, without the consent of the

holders of two-thirds of the outstanding shares of each class of preferred stock, no

additional preferred stock may be issued unless the Company’s gross income (determined

in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles) for a specified twelve-

month period is at least 1-1/2 times the interest for one year on all long-term debt of the

Company and the dividend requirements on all preferred stock of the Company that will

be outstanding after the issuance of the preferred stock proposed to be issued.

        After dividends on all classes and series of preferred stock have been paid (or

declared and set apart for payment) for all past dividend periods and declared for the

current dividend period, at the full rates fixed therefore, dividends may be declared and

paid on the common stock of the Company subject to the restrictions set forth below.




1
       See Westar Energy, Inc., 102 FERC ¶ 61,186 at PP 20-21 (2003), order on clarification, 104
FERC ¶ 61,018 (2003).



                                                  9
        Under the Company’s certificate of incorporation, if any shares of its preferred

stock are outstanding, dividends (other than dividends payable in common stock),

distributions or acquisitions of the Company common stock:

   •   may not exceed 50 percent of net income for a prior 12-month period, after

       deducting dividends on any preferred stock during the period, if the sum of the

       capital represented by the common stock, premiums on capital, and surplus

       accounts is less than 20 percent of capitalization;

   •   may not exceed 75 percent of net income for such 12-month period, as adjusted if

       this capitalization ratio is 20 percent or more, but less than 25 percent; and

   •   if this capitalization ratio exceeds 25 percent, dividends, distributions or

       acquisitions may not reduce the ratio to less than 25 percent except to the extent

       permitted by the provisions described in the above two bullet points.

       No portion of the retained earnings of the Company is presently restricted by this

provision. The Restated Certificate of Incorporation further provides that no dividends

may be declared or paid on the common stock until all amounts required to be paid or set

aside for any sinking fund for the redemption or purchase of Cumulative Preferred Stock,

par value $25 per share, have been paid or set aside. Currently, no shares of Cumulative

Preferred Stock, par value $25 per share, are outstanding.

       Pursuant to the leverage restriction in the Company’s revolving credit agreement,

the Company must also maintain a percentage of debt to total capitalization at a level that

does not exceed 65 percent. The payment of cash dividends indirectly results in an

increase in the percentage of debt to total capitalization, which results in the restriction of

approximately $946.7 million of the Company’s retained earnings from being paid out as




                                              10
 dividends. Accordingly, approximately $3.2 billion of the Company’s retained earnings

as of June 30, 2026 are unrestricted for the payment of dividends.

(j)    A brief summary of any rate changes which were made effective during the
       period for which financial statements are submitted or which became or will
       become effective after the period for which statements are submitted:

       (1)     Completed Regulatory Matters

Integrated Resource Plans

       In 2025, the Company issued its 2025 integrated resource plan (“IRP”) to the

OCC and APSC. The 2025 IRP intended to address updated planning assumptions from

the Company’s 2024 IRP and present the Company’s current capacity needs in light of

the Southwest Power Pool, Inc.’s (“SPP”) planning reserve margin requirements for both

summer and winter seasons as well as the SPP’s revised resource accreditation

methodologies and updated load projections. The 2025 IRP identified capacity needs of

1,647 megawatts (“MWs”) by 2030. The Company has executed contracts for nearly

1,000 MWs of generation as a result of the 2024 request for proposal process, and

regulatory approvals are currently being pursued, as further discussed below. Further, in

January 2026, the Company issued additional requests for proposals for resources to meet

projected capacity needs while maintaining affordability and reliability for the

Company’s customers. In April 2026, the Company issued its final 2026 IRP to the OCC

and APSC, which is intended to address the Company’s updated load forecast as well as

updated SPP Resource Adequacy policies. The 2026 IRP identifies capacity needs of

1,922 MWs by the 2031/2032 winter season, which is inclusive of approximately 800

MWs of capacity needs driven by changes in the SPP Resource Adequacy policies. The

Company intends to evaluate incremental capacity needs through future IRPs and to

continue to seek capacity additions, as needed.


                                            11
 APSC Proceedings

2025 Arkansas Act 373 Tariff Filing

       In December 2025, the Company filed an application for approval of an Act 373 6

tariff to recover return on construction work in progress (“CWIP”) and revenue

requirement for the generating units being constructed at Horseshoe Lake (Units 11 and

12) and Tinker Air Force Base. Recovery under the Act 373 tariff is dependent on a

finding of eligibility for the Horseshoe Lake Units 11 and 12 and Tinker generation

facilities in the prudence case described below. In April 2026, the APSC issued an order

approving the Company’s Act 373 tariff.

Arkansas Prudence of Horseshoe Lake and Tinker Generation Facilities

       In December 2024, pursuant to orders in the generation construction notice

filings, the Company filed an application requesting a determination of prudence of

action and initial contract costs for the generating units being constructed at Horseshoe

Lake (Units 11 and 12) and Tinker Air Force Base. In May 2025, intervenors, including

the Attorney General, filed direct testimony and APSC staff recommended a finding of

prudence of action and initial contract costs for both projects. The Attorney General

recommended approval of the Horseshoe Lake project but raised concerns regarding

certain elements of the Tinker Air Force Base project. In May 2025, the Company filed a

supplemental application to serve as notice to the APSC of the Company’s intent to

recover the costs of these projects through a rider under the newly enacted Act 373. In

June 2025, the Company filed rebuttal testimony to address concerns raised by the

Attorney General in direct testimony. The Company entered into a settlement agreement



6
       See Arkansas 95th Gen. Assembly, Regular Session, 2025, Act 373 (March 11, 2025).


                                               12
 with APSC Staff in August 2025 providing that the Horseshoe Lake and Tinker

combustion turbines were prudent and that the Company satisfied part of the eligibility

criteria for recovery of these costs through a Strategic Investment Rider. The Arkansas

Attorney General opposed the part of the settlement relating to eligibility for a Strategic

Investment Rider. In August 2025, the APSC issued an order seeking additional

testimony that responds to several questions related to the eligibility of the Strategic

Investment Rider for out-of-state projects. In September 2025, the Company and APSC

Staff filed responsive supplemental testimony. On September 9, 2026, the APSC issued a

final order approving the prudence of action and initial costs of both the Horseshoe Lake

and Tinker Air Force Base generating facilities. The APSC denied the portion of the

settlement which would have made the facilities eligible for recovery through the

Generating Arkansas Jobs Act Rider.

Arkansas Frontier Energy Storage Project Preapproval Filing

       In February 2026, the Company filed a preapproval case for the Frontier Energy

Storage Project, which involves a purchase and sale agreement for a 300 MW battery

storage facility in Oklahoma. The Frontier Energy Storage Project is the final project

resulting from the Company’s 2024 request for proposals and subsequent negotiations.

In this proceeding, the Company sought authorization to commence construction of the

Frontier Energy Storage Project and to later acquire the facility pursuant to the purchase

and sale agreement, a prudency determination for the project, and all other findings and

approvals needed under Arkansas law. In April 2026, the APSC Staff and the Attorney

General filed direct testimony recommending approval of the Frontier Energy Storage

Project, subject to certain conditions. In May 2026, a non-contested settlement was




                                             13
 reached between the APSC Staff and the Company. In June 2026, the APSC issued an

order requesting briefs on certain issues, including regarding whether a battery is a

generating facility, and intervenors subsequently filed their briefs. On July 31, 2026, the

APSC issued an order approving the non-contested settlement, finding the decision to

acquire the project and the initial costs are prudent.

OCC Proceedings

Oklahoma Frontier Energy Storage Project Preapproval Filing

       In December 2025, the Company filed a preapproval case for the Frontier Energy

Storage Project. In January 2026, the Attorney General and Petroleum Alliance of

Oklahoma filed a joint motion to dismiss the case based on an interpretation that a battery

energy storage system is not an electric generation facility. In February 2026, the

Company filed a response in opposition to the joint motion to dismiss, and in April 2026,

the administrative law judge (“ALJ”) issued a report that recommended the OCC deny

the joint motion to dismiss. In June 2026, the ALJ issued a report recommending

approval of the Frontier Energy Storage Project, with rider recovery limited to 18 months

after the project is placed in service. The ALJ report does not allow for a tariff

contingency to be collected through the rider but otherwise adopts the Company’s

positions in the case. The Attorney General subsequently filed exceptions to the ALJ

report, and the Company filed a response to the Attorney General’s exceptions. On

August 6, 2026, the OCC issued an order preapproving the Frontier Energy Storage

Project.




                                              14
 Oklahoma Distribution Interconnection Agreement

       In May 2026, the Company filed an application requesting approval of a pro

forma Distribution Interconnection Agreement to be used for certain interconnections to

the Company’s distribution system for generators that do not have a purchase agreement

for the output with the Company and are larger than 300kW. On July 16, 2026, the ALJ

recommended approval of the Company’s application. On August 6, 2026, the OCC

issued an order approving the Company’s application.

       (2)     Pending Regulatory Matters

       Various proceedings pending before state or federal regulatory agencies are

described below. Unless stated otherwise, the Company cannot predict when the

regulatory agency will act or what action the regulatory agency will take. The

Company’s financial results are dependent in part on timely and constructive decisions by

the regulatory agencies that set the Company’s rates.

SPP Proceedings

Demand Response Accreditation

       SPP has been evaluating demand response accreditation for several years, and a

proposal has evolved that would treat demand resource accreditation on a performance-

based approach. This approach requires demand response resources to be market

registered and dispatched based on SPP market protocols or be reliability registered and

dispatched during conservative operations or energy emergency alerts within SPP.

Alternatively, demand response programs that are built into a Load Responsible Entity’s

(“LRE”) forecast, known as load modifiers, can be used to reduce the load and resources

needed to satisfy the entity’s planning reserve margin but would include an after-the-fact




                                            15
 look at whether the LRE’s peak forecast was below the actuals in a given year. If under

forecasted, a LRE would have to pay a deficiency payment for not providing enough

resources to satisfy its planning reserve margin and actual peak load. At their February

2026 meetings, both the SPP Regional State Committee and SPP Board of Directors

adopted policies to include the 2027 implementation of a LRE’s load modifier cap and

full implementation in 2028. These policies are subject to FERC review and approval

prior to implementation.

Seminole to Shreveport Transmission Line

       At the end of 2025, the SPP Board of Directors adopted their 2025 Integrated

Transmission Plan. This plan included a new 765kV transmission line running from

Konawa, Oklahoma to Shreveport, Louisiana. The Company will construct and own a

significant portion of the line. The project is pending the Company’s receipt and

acceptance of a notice to construct, which is expected later this year.

APSC Proceedings

2025 Arkansas Preapproval Case

       In July 2025, the Company filed an application requesting several approvals from

the APSC relating to three capacity projects arising from the 2024 request for proposals

for generating capacity: (i) the Black Kettle Battery Storage capacity purchase agreement

(“CPA”); (ii) the Kiamichi natural gas CPA; and (iii) the construction of two additional

combustion turbines at the Horseshoe Lake generating facility (Units 13 and 14). The

Company sought authority to begin construction of the Horseshoe Lake units, a prudency

determination of those new Horseshoe Lake units, authorization to enter into the Black

Kettle Battery Storage CPA and other findings needed under Arkansas law, including




                                             16
 eligibility to recover costs of the new Horseshoe Lake units through a rider under Act

373. In November 2025, the Company and the APSC staff filed a settlement agreement

approving the Company’s application with some additional reporting requirements and

allowing an additional return on the Black Kettle Battery Storage CPA at the 20-year

U.S. treasury rate. In December 2025, the Attorney General filed testimony in opposition

to the settlement. In January 2026, the APSC issued an order denying the settlement

agreement and denying preapproval of Horseshoe Lake Units 13 and 14 but approving

the Black Kettle Battery Storage CPA. The APSC also found that the Company did not

need to seek approval of the Kiamichi natural gas CPA since the term is shorter than five

years. In the order, the APSC stated the Company could still seek a prudence

determination and cost recovery of Horseshoe Lake Units 13 and 14 after they are placed

into service. In February 2026, the Company filed additional evidence pursuant to

Arkansas law and requested that the APSC consider the additional evidence in finding

that Horseshoe Lake Units 13 and 14 are reasonable, necessary and in the public interest.

In March 2026, the APSC issued an order that again declined to grant prudence of

Horseshoe Lake Units 13 and 14 but clarified that the Company is authorized to begin

construction and the APSC’s previous order should not be construed to indicate prudence

or imprudence. The APSC re-stated that the Company may request approval for

Horseshoe Lake Units 13 and 14 in a future rate case. Parties have filed comments in

response to questions posed by the APSC’s March 2026 order, and the Company is

awaiting further action from the APSC.




                                           17
 Arkansas Long-term CPAs

       In July 2026, the Company filed its application and direct testimony to seek

approval for two long-term CPAs as presented in the Oklahoma Google special contract

case, which is described further below.

FERC Proceedings

Order for Sponsored Transmission Upgrades within SPP

       Under Attachment Z2 of the SPP Open Access Transmission Tariff (“OATT”),

the Company and others who built participant-funded, or “sponsored,” transmission

upgrades may recover the costs of the upgrade from other SPP customers who benefit

from it. FERC approved a waiver of a time limitation in the SPP OATT to allow the SPP

in 2016 to bill for the 2008 through 2015 period due to information system limitations

that had delayed that billing. SPP then both billed users and credited sponsors, including

the Company, for Z2 charges during the period. The Company refunded most of the net

credits to customers through its various rate riders that include SPP activity and retained

the remaining amounts.

       Net payers of Z2 credits contested the waiver, leading FERC to reverse its

decision, deny the waiver, and instruct the SPP to refund payments made for charges

from 2008 to 2015. The Company and other net creditors challenged this reversal.

However, FERC upheld its reversal, and in August 2021 and September 2024, the U.S.

Court of Appeals upheld FERC’s decision and denied relief to the Company and the other

creditors against SPP. All appellate options have now been exhausted.

       On July 16, 2026, the FERC ordered the SPP to begin invoicing the Company and

other parties by August 17, 2026, for refund amounts owed. SPP must begin distributing




                                             18
 refunds to project users once it has received the funds. SPP must also submit a refund

report within 60 days after issuing the initial invoices, including the recoupment amounts

and complete interest calculations. SPP previously calculated that the Company will

need to refund approximately $14 million, net of the amounts the Company paid to other

utilities for upgrades, plus interest. This order will shift recovery of these upgrade credits

to future periods. Of the approximately $14 million refund amount, the Company

recognized approximately $4 million in expense in 2021 that initially benefited the

Company in 2016, and the Company’s customers will incur a net impact of

approximately $10 million in expense through rider mechanisms or the FERC formula

rate once the refunds occur. As of June 30, 2026, the Company has reserved $14 million

plus estimated interest for a potential refund.

       After the initiation of the disputes described above, FERC approved an SPP

proposal to eliminate Attachment Z2 revenue crediting and replace it with a different rate

mechanism that would provide project sponsors, such as the Company, the same level of

recovery. This elimination of the Attachment Z2 revenue crediting would only impact

the Company and its recovery of any future upgrade costs that it may incur as a project

sponsor after July 2020. All projects initiated prior to July 2020 remain eligible to

receive revenue credits under Attachment Z2, which includes the $14 million related to

the refunds discussed above.

OCC Proceedings

Oklahoma CWIP Filing

       In December 2025, the Company filed an application for CWIP treatment for

Horseshoe Lake combustion turbines Units 13 and 14, as allowed by Oklahoma Senate




                                             19
 Bill 998. A motion to dismiss the case was filed by the Oklahoma Industrial Energy

Consumers, as well as the Public Utility Division Staff. The Company filed a response as

well as motions to move the case and all outstanding motions to be heard en banc. These

motions were heard before the OCC in January 2026. In March 2026, the OCC issued an

order dismissing the case, and on the same day, the Company filed an appeal at the

Oklahoma Supreme Court. The case is now fully briefed and is awaiting a decision from

the Oklahoma Supreme Court.

Oklahoma 2025 Fuel Prudence

       In April 2026, the Public Utility Division Staff filed their application initiating the

prudence review of the 2025 fuel adjustment clause. The Company filed its direct

testimony and minimum filing requirements in June 2026. A hearing is scheduled for

October 8, 2026.

Oklahoma Google Special Contract

       In May 2026, the Company filed an application requesting approval of a special

contract with Google and preapproval of two CPAs. The special contract includes

provisions such as long-term contract commitments, minimum billing demand and

energy charges, funding of upfront costs, and recognizing OCC authority to review and

address any potential adverse rate impact in future rate proceedings through cost-of-

service adjustments. Further, as part of the special contract, the Company secured power

generation capacity agreements from two solar facilities that Google currently has under

construction. Intervenors filed Responsive Testimony on August 5, 2026, and the

Company filed Rebuttal Testimony on August 21, 2026. On September 9, 2026, a non-

contested settlement was reached, and a hearing on the settlement was held the same day.




                                             20
 At the conclusion of the hearing, the ALJ recommended approval of the settlement. The

Company is awaiting a final order from the Commission.

Oklahoma Large Load Tariff

          In June 2026, the Company filed an application requesting approval of its new

proposed Extra Large Power and Light (“XLPL”) tariff and terms and conditions of

service for extra large load customers and for approval of a regulatory asset to recover

costs associated with portfolio optimization software. If approved, the XLPL tariff would

establish a framework to serve large load customers (75 MWs or higher) and include

provisions such as long-term contract commitments, minimum billing demand and

energy charges, funding of upfront costs, a customer protection charge that addresses any

potential adverse rate impact to other customer classes, and a customer affordability

charge that would be credited to residential customers through a regulatory liability. A

hearing is scheduled for November 3, 2026.

Oklahoma Muskogee County Bond Refinance

      On August 27, 2026, the Company filed an application to refinance up to $56

million of Muskogee County pollution control bonds. The Company is awaiting a

procedural schedule.

necessary or advisable, provided that the aggregate amount of all such short-term
borrowings in the name of the Company outstanding and remaining unpaid at any
time during the period ending December 31, 2028, shall not exceed
$1,500,000,000.

officers of this Company be and they are hereby authorized and empowered, for
and in the name of this Company: (a) to issue promissory notes to financial
institutions and other entities, provided that the note or notes or instruments of
renewal evidencing each borrowing or its renewal shall mature not more than
twelve months from the date of the borrowing or renewal; (b) to issue promissory
notes to or through commercial paper dealers, each such note to mature not more
than twelve months from the date of issuance and to bear interest rates dependent
